title: Trump Floats Ted Cruz for Supreme Court, Joking Bipartisan Dislike Guarantees 100 Votes
snippet: At a Texas rally, Donald Trump joked that Sen. Ted Cruz would easily win Supreme Court confirmation because lawmakers in both parties would vote for him just to get him out of the Senate.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump offered a lighthearted solution to potential Senate confirmation battles over future Supreme Court vacancies: nominate Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, because lawmakers from both sides of the aisle would eagerly vote to send him to the bench just to clear him out of the Capitol.

Speaking at a midterm campaign rally in Lubbock, Texas, Trump joked that selecting the third-term conservative firebrand would yield a rare, unanimous consensus in the upper chamber.

"I would pick Ted Cruz to be the next Supreme Court justice, and I wouldn't have to worry about it. I wouldn't have to make a phone call," Trump told the crowd. "The Democrats will 100% vote for it because they hate the guy and they want to get rid of him. And the Republicans would 100% vote for it because they can't stand him... So I'd get 100% of the vote, and he would be a Supreme Court justice and he'd do a great job."

A Formidable Legal Resume Meets Political Ambition

Cruz, who was seated in the front row at the event, smiled and laughed as Trump delivered the punchline. Despite Trump praising him as a "brilliant lawyer," Cruz has repeatedly brushed off the idea of joining the High Court. "I don't want to be a judge," Cruz noted in a September interview.

Despite his reluctance, Cruz possesses extensive legal credentials. A graduate of Harvard Law School, Cruz clerked for former Chief Justice William Rehnquist and served as Texas Solicitor General from 2008 to 2013, during which he argued several high-profile cases before the Supreme Court.

Buyer's Remorse and 2028 Political Calculations

Trump's musings follow his public expressions of regret regarding his three first-term Supreme Court appointments—Justices Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett—after they sided against his administration in a series of key legal rulings.

Elevating Cruz to the judiciary could also alter the landscape for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination. Cruz, who ran against Trump in 2016, has made no secret of his ongoing interest in the White House, where he would potentially face off against fellow conservatives like Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Sidelining Cruz on the bench would narrow that primary field.

However, it remains uncertain whether Trump will even have the chance to name a fourth justice. Conservative Justice Samuel Alito recently dispelled rumors of an impending retirement, confirming he intends to remain on the bench through at least the upcoming session.
